metadata.title: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Management of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
metadata.organization: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)

epidemiology.global_burden: HCC is the sixth most common cancer and third leading cause of cancer death
epidemiology.incidence: More than 900,000 new cases annually worldwide

viral.hbv: Leading cause globally; can cause HCC without cirrhosis
viral.hcv: Major cause in developed countries; risk persists after SVR

non_viral.nafld_mash: Increasingly common cause, especially in Western countries
non_viral.alcohol: Major risk factor; synergistic with viral hepatitis

recommendation.population: Patients with cirrhosis of any aetiology who are fit for treatment
Non-cirrhotic chronic HBV with high risk (F3 fibrosis, family history)

afp.utility: May add sensitivity to US but limited specificity
afp.recommendation: Consider adding AFP in selected cases, particularly if high pre-test probability

surveillance.exclusion: Child-Pugh C not listed for transplantation

us_quality.visualization: Inadequate visualization in 20% of cirrhotic patients
us_quality.alternative: Consider CT or abbreviated MRI if US quality inadequate

recommendation.description: Non-invasive diagnosis using contrast-enhanced CT or MRI in cirrhotic patients
recommendation.criteria: Arterial phase hyperenhancement with washout on portal venous/delayed phase
recommendation.size: Applicable for nodules 1 cm or greater

li_rads.lr5: Definite HCC - no biopsy needed in cirrhosis
li_rads.lr4: Probable HCC - close follow-up or biopsy
li_rads.lr_m: Malignant, not specific for HCC - biopsy recommended

biopsy.immunostaining: HSP70, glypican-3, glutamine synthetase for early/well-differentiated HCC

biomarkers.afp: Not sufficient alone; useful adjunct in appropriate clinical context
biomarkers.emerging: Liquid biopsy, methylation markers under investigation

recommendation.description: BCLC 2022 staging system recommended for prognosis and treatment allocation

stage.name: A
stage.tumor: Single any size or up to 3 nodules up to 3 cm

liver_function.albi: ALBI grade provides additional objective stratification

portal_hypertension.hvpg: HVPG greater than or equal to 10 mmHg indicates clinically significant PH
portal_hypertension.baveno_vii: Updated criteria for non-invasive PH assessment

recommendation.indication: BCLC 0/A with preserved liver function, no clinically significant portal hypertension

recommendation.description: Portal hypertension is a relative but not absolute contraindication

portal_hypertension.selected_cases: Limited resections may be performed with HVPG 10-12 mmHg

laparoscopic.recommendation: Minimally invasive approach preferred when feasible

surgical_resection.future_liver_remnant: At least 40% FLR for cirrhotic patients

recommendation.description: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab may be considered for high-risk HCC after resection/ablation

imb.high_risk_criteria: Microvascular invasion, poor differentiation, tumors greater than 5 cm, multiple tumors

recommendation.indication: BCLC A with decompensated cirrhosis or clinically significant portal hypertension within transplant criteria

criteria.milan: Single up to 5 cm or 2-3 up to 3 cm each, no vascular invasion

extended.ucsf: Single up to 6.5 cm or 2-3 with largest up to 4.5 cm, total up to 8 cm

recommendation.description: Downstaging should be offered to selected patients beyond criteria

downstaging.xxl_trial: Positive RCT for downstaging followed by LT vs alternative treatment
downstaging.observation: 3-6 months post-downstaging to assess tumor biology

recommendation.description: Locoregional therapy recommended for expected wait time greater than 6 months
ICIs before transplant may be considered but require caution due to rejection risk

ici_bridging.washout: Adequate washout period recommended before transplantation

mtor_inhibitors.silver_trial: Sirolimus reduced recurrence in patients with active tumors at explant
mtor_inhibitors.recommendation: Consider mTOR inhibitors for high-risk patients

ici_contraindicated.recommendation: ICIs NOT recommended post-transplant due to high rejection risk

recommendation.indication: BCLC 0/A, tumors up to 3 cm, not surgical candidates

modalities.rfa: Standard for tumors less than 3 cm
modalities.mwa: May be superior for 3-5 cm; less heat-sink effect

outcomes.complete_ablation: Greater than 90% for tumors less than 3 cm

ablation.combination_tace: May improve outcomes for larger tumors (3-5 cm)

recommendation.description: SBRT is an alternative when ablation not feasible

sbrt.bridge_to_transplant: Comparable to TACE/RFA as bridge therapy

recommendation.indication: BCLC B (intermediate stage) with preserved liver function

techniques.tae: Bland embolization - comparable in some studies

recommendation.description: Transition to systemic therapy after TACE failure (2 non-responding sessions or stage progression)
TACE plus ICI combinations may be considered for selected patients
TARE is an alternative to TACE for intermediate-stage HCC

dosimetry.dosisphere_01: Personalized dosimetry (greater than 205 Gy) improves outcomes
dosimetry.orr: 76.6% vs 22.2% with personalized vs standard dosimetry

tare.pvt: May be used with segmental/lobar portal vein invasion

radiation_segmentectomy.raser_study: Curative intent for very early to early HCC

versus_tace.trace_trial: No OS difference; improved TTP with TARE

recommendation.description: Combination therapy with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors recommended for advanced HCC

atezolizumab_bevacizumab.indication: BCLC C or TACE-refractory, Child-Pugh A
atezolizumab_bevacizumab.requirement: Upper endoscopy within 6 months; adequate variceal treatment

durvalumab_tremelimumab.regimen: STRIDE: Tremelimumab 300 mg single dose plus durvalumab, then durvalumab q4w
durvalumab_tremelimumab.durvalumab_monotherapy: Non-inferior to sorafenib; alternative if anti-CTLA4 not suitable

recommendation.description: Aetiology should NOT influence systemic therapy choice

aetiology.meta_analysis: ICI benefit confirmed across all aetiologies including non-viral

recommendation.description: TKI recommended after progression on ICI-based combinations

cabozantinib.post_ici: Emerging data supports activity after ICI

ramucirumab.indication: AFP greater than or equal to 400 ng/mL

recommendation.description: Systemic therapy not routinely recommended outside trials, but Child-Pugh B7-B8 may be considered case-by-case
Sorafenib/lenvatinib may be considered; ICIs NOT recommended

post_transplant_recurrence.ici_rejection_risk: High risk of graft rejection with checkpoint inhibitors

recommendation.description: Local therapy may be considered while continuing systemic treatment for oligoprogression
Discontinuation after sustained response (greater than or equal to 2 years) may be discussed with patient
May continue treatment if clinical benefit is observed
RECIST v1.1 as primary assessment for systemic therapy trials

response_assessment.mrecist: May provide complementary information, especially for locoregional therapy

recommendation.description: OS should remain primary endpoint for RCTs in HCC

after_curative_treatment.imaging: CT or MRI every 3-4 months for 2 years, then every 6 months
after_curative_treatment.afp: Every 3-4 months if elevated at baseline

recommendation.description: Clinical evaluation and CT/MRI every 3-4 months

palliative_care.indication: BCLC D, Child-Pugh C not for transplant, PS greater than 2

key_recommendations.recommendation: ICI-based combination therapy for advanced HCC (100% consensus)
Aetiology should not influence therapy choice (100% consensus)
TKI after ICI-based combination failure (100% consensus)
Child-Pugh B may be considered case-by-case (100% consensus)
RECIST v1.1 for systemic therapy assessment (92% consensus)
OS as primary endpoint for RCTs (100% consensus)
Treatment beyond progression if clinical benefit (87% consensus)
